amendment_history.date_hijri: غير مؤكد (لكنه سابق لـ 1432هـ/2011م، بدليل نسخة nshr.org.sa)
amendment_history.note: لم يُعثر هذه الجولة على رقم/تاريخ القرار الوزاري التأسيسي الذي أصدر اللائحة التنفيذية لأول مرة عملا بالمادة 43 من النظام. مسجل صراحة كفجوة غير مؤكدة.

amendment_history.decree: نسخة موثقة عبر الجمعية الوطنية لحقوق الإنسان (nshr.org.sa)، بلا رقم قرار مذكور صراحة على الغلاف
amendment_history.date_hijri: 1432هـ - 2011م (تاريخ الغلاف؛ تاريخ إنشاء ملف PDF: 4 يونيو 2012م)
amendment_history.note: نسخة أقدم من هذا الكتيب المُدمج (النظام + لائحته)، تستخدم صيغة ترقيم مختلفة لفقرات اللائحة ('ن/مل') عن صيغة الإصدار الثالث ('ن-م'). تُستخدم هنا كنقطة مقارنة تاريخية جزئية، وليست نصا مُدرجا في هذا المسار.

الرقم/التاريخ المذكوران صراحة على غلاف الملف الأساسي المعتمد لهذا المسار (moh.gov.sa، الملف الأساسي: Executive-Regulations-Health-Profession-1.pdf). يُرجَّح -- بالنظر لوجود نسخة 2011 السابقة له بسنوات -- أنه قرار إعادة إصدار/تحديث للائحة قائمة أصلا، لا قرار الإصدار التأسيسي المطلق؛ انظر healthcare_professions_regulation_founding_resolution_uncertain.

النسخة المُدرجة في هذا المسار، مؤكدة بصريا على غلاف نسخة ثانية مستقلة من ملف وزارة الصحة نفسه (executive-regulations-health-profession.pdf، بلا لاحقة '-1'، منتج مختلف iLovePDF، 39 صفحة): 'الإصدار الثالث 1440هـ - 2019م'.

verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE ACCESS: fetched the exact PDF URL given as this track's starting point -- https://www.moh.gov.sa/Ministry/Rules/Documents/Executive-Regulations-Health-Profession-1.pdf -- directly via curl this pass: HTTP 200, 1,119,546 bytes, 32 pages, Adobe InDesign CC 13.0, created 2018-02-12 (this creation date sits within roughly one month of an independently located Arabic news article (sabq.org) describing this same consolidated Law+Regulation booklet's Official Gazette (Umm al-Qura) publication on 2018-03-16, i.e. ~27/6/1439H -- consistent timing, not identical, since gazette publication typically trails ministerial approval and file compilation by some weeks). This exact byte sequence was independently re-confirmed via TWO further channels: (a) the Wayback Machine's archived snapshot of this same URL (timestamp 20250805233027, fetched via https://web.archive.org/web/<ts>/<url> -- https scheme succeeded HTTP 200, http scheme returned HTTP 403, consistent with this corpus's established per-snapshot scheme variability) is BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 d6d5702b4806ed5c0975bb0ce6c4db36) to the live fetch; archive.org/wayback/available's CDX metadata API worked directly, while web.archive.org's CDX *search* endpoint (web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx) was blocked by this environment's egress policy -- only the content-serving snapshot URL and the lightweight 'available' lookup worked, matching this task's own advance warning; (b) a third-party mirror, docdroid.net (docdroid.net/file/download/ssorNXL/...), hosting what is a byte-identical re-upload of the same PDF (identical md5), confirming the file has not been silently altered at its primary host. A SECOND, independently-produced MOH export of the same regulation -- moh.gov.sa/ministry/rules/documents/executive-regulations-health-profession.pdf (note: no '-1' suffix, different producer 'iLovePDF', different pagination, 39 pages incl. an added social-media letterhead footer on every page) -- explicitly labels itself on its own cover page 'الإصدار الثالث 1440هـ - 2019م' ('3rd edition, 1440H-2019'); this label is not visible anywhere on the primary '-1' file's own pages, but the two files were directly, programmatically cross-compared paragraph-by-paragraph after independent text extraction (see EXTRACTION METHODOLOGY below) and found to carry the same law-article/regulation-paragraph content, confirming the primary file is this same 3rd (2019/1440H) edition. CROSS-CHECK ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED THIS PASS: laws.boe.gov.sa (direct curl to the domain root returned 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer', matching this corpus's established pattern for this domain when unreachable, and WebFetch on the base law's own known BOE lawId page returned HTTP 503); ncar.gov.sa (direct curl returned the same connection-reset error, and WebFetch on a specific NCAR document-details URL located via web search -- whose title, 'اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الصحية لعام 1439هـ', independently corroborates this track's 1439H dating -- returned HTTP 503). Both are consistent with this corpus's documented precedent that BOE does not maintain separate lawId records for ministerial-resolution-level Implementing Regulations (as opposed to laws/royal decrees), and that ncar.gov.sa's document-details pages are frequently unreachable via automated fetch even when discoverable via web search. qanoniah.com was reachable at its domain root (HTTP 200) but, consistent with this corpus's documented finding for the same domain in the anti_smoking_regulation and traffic_regulation tracks, was not individually re-fetched for a page specific to this regulation this pass -- not claimed as a cross-check here. r.jina.ai was attempted as a reader-proxy fallback for the BOE lawId page and returned HTTP 401 ('blocked from performing anonymous queries due to bad IP reputation'), consistent with this task's advance warning about this environment's outbound path.

EDITION HISTORY -- A GENUINELY EARLIER SOURCE LOCATED: a PDF hosted by the National Society for Human Rights (nshr.org.sa/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/529_PDF1.pdf), an independent quasi-governmental human-rights body unrelated to MOH, titled 'نظام مزاولة المهن الصحية ولائحته التنفيذية 1432هـ - 2011م', was fetched directly (HTTP 200) and its text extracted. This is a genuinely EARLIER edition of this same consolidated Law+Regulation booklet, predating the 3rd (2019/1440H) edition by roughly eight years. It uses a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT regulation-paragraph numbering convention -- 'N/Mل' (e.g. '9/2ل', '1/22ل', '4/35ل') -- versus the 3rd edition's 'N-M' convention (e.g. '8-2', '1-22'... where such paragraphs exist), and at least one directly-observed renumbering: the 2011 edition's '9/2ل' paragraph (experience-requirement text for government-employed practitioners) reads essentially verbatim to the 3rd edition's '8-2' paragraph, but under a DIFFERENT sequence number, implying at least one paragraph was inserted, removed, or reordered earlier in article 2's regulation list between 2011 and 2019. This track does NOT claim an exhaustive, paragraph-by-paragraph diff of all 44 articles between the 2011 and 2019 texts (that would require the same scale of careful cross-reading as this pass's own primary-text extraction, and was not completed to that depth this pass) -- this is disclosed as a scope limitation, not silently assumed away. What IS confirmed: (a) the numbering-CONVENTION itself changed between editions; (b) at least the article-2 content sampled is substantively continuous across both editions; (c) the 2011 edition ALSO documents, in the same abortion-related article (law article 22), a citation to 'قرار هيئة كبار العلماء رقم 140 وتاريخ 1404/7/29هـ' (Senior Ulema Council decision), a citation this track's own extraction of the 3rd edition independently reproduces verbatim for the same article -- corroborating that this specific Sharia-council citation has been stable across at least these two editions.

EXTRACTION METHODOLOGY (why this was hard, and how it was solved without fabrication): pdftotext -- both '-layout' and plain modes -- on the primary MOH PDF was tried first and largely succeeded, BUT systematically split individual justified (kashida-stretched) words across a stray inserted space wherever the source PDF's own decorative tatweel run crossed a word boundary (e.g. 'توصياتها' emerging as 'توصياته ا'), corrupting dozens of words per page -- an artifact, not a content difference (matches this corpus's own prior documented finding, in the anti_smoking_regulation track, that this exact MOH PDF file family resists clean pdftotext extraction). Switching to PyMuPDF's word-box extraction (get_text('words')) with explicit RTL reordering (grouping words by line, then sorting each line's words by descending x-coordinate) fixed this: every word came through as a single intact token (only cosmetic decorative tatweel U+0640 characters remaining, stripped outright as this corpus already does elsewhere). Two remaining, fully mechanical bidi artifacts were found and corrected, BOTH verified via codepoint inspection (not guessed): (1) leading punctuation and tanween-fatha marks were consistently glued to the FRONT of the following token instead of the END of the preceding token (a bidi mirroring artifact of the extraction, not a content choice) -- corrected by moving any leading '، . : ؛ ً ٌ ٍ' from a token's front to its own end; (2) MOST CONSEQUENTIALLY, this specific PDF's embedded font's ToUnicode/CMap table maps the mandatory lam-alef ligature glyph (ل immediately followed by ا) inconsistently: when the ligature falls at the START of an isolated two-letter word (the negation particle 'لا'), both characters survive but in SWAPPED order (yielding 'ال', indistinguishable in isolation from the definite article -- resolved contextually, since in every single instance located in this regulation's text the swapped token is immediately followed by a verb, never a noun, which is how the genuine definite article can never behave); when the SAME ligature falls mid-word, the lam is dropped OUTRIGHT, collapsing e.g. 'علاقة' to 'عاقة', 'ثلاثة' to 'ثاثة', 'اللائحة' itself to 'الائحة', 'خلال' to 'خال'. This is a genuine, disclosed defect in the SOURCE PDF's own font encoding, not an artifact of one extraction tool: it was independently confirmed to affect BOTH of the MOH-hosted PDF exports identically (e.g. 'العلاقة' and 'ثلاثة' occur ZERO times, correctly spelled, anywhere in either 1,119,546-byte or 279,549-byte MOH file, while their broken forms occur consistently and exclusively), so switching extraction tool alone cannot fix it. It was corrected via a small, closed, individually-justified word list (each entry verified against its actual surrounding sentence context, e.g. 'العلاجية' confirmed by 'الإجراءات العلاجية' / 'الخطة العلاجية' appearing in an unmistakably medical-treatment context, never the unrelated word 'عاجل' (urgent) or 'عاقل' (sane), which are genuinely, correctly spelled elsewhere in this same text and were correspondingly left untouched) -- restoring the single dropped or reordered ligature letter, never altering any other letter, word choice, or legal meaning. Two further page-layout artifacts (not ligature-related) were found and excised, both fully disclosed in known_unresolved_discrepancies below: an editorial footnote spliced mid-sentence into article 35's third اللائحة paragraph at a page-break boundary, and trailing فصل/فرع heading text (plus, in one case, that heading's own footnote marker) appended to the LAST اللائحة paragraph of each article that happens to be the final article of its فصل or فرع (articles 4, 14, 23, 25, 41) -- a scrape-boundary artifact of the same kind already documented elsewhere in this corpus (e.g. the base healthcare_professions_law track's own nezams.com article-44 boundary-artifact discrepancy), not a content difference. All decorative tatweel (kashida) and all residual tashkeel (tanween/fatha/damma/kasra/shadda) were stripped uniformly across this track's text, consistent with the majority convention already documented across this corpus (see e.g. the anti_smoking_regulation track's own methodology note), given this source PDF's demonstrated inability to encode tanween reliably (120 of 127 tanween-fatha occurrences in the raw extraction were missing their required carrying alef -- a defect, not a content signal worth preserving unreliably).

SCOPE: this track ingests ONLY the اللائحة (regulation) paragraphs -- the base 44-article Law's own text is already tracked separately at sources/healthcare_professions/ and is NOT duplicated here. Of the Law's 44 articles, 30 carry at least one numbered اللائحة paragraph in this 3rd edition; 14 do not (articles 6, 13, 21, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 42, 43 -- concentrated almost entirely in the civil/penal/disciplinary-liability chapter, articles 26-32, and the closing-provisions chapter, articles 42-44 minus 44 itself, plus three isolated short articles 6/13/21 whose one-sentence law text apparently needed no further elaboration in this edition). This absence is a structural fact of the primary source, not an extraction gap -- confirmed by the presence of an unambiguous 'الالئحة:'/'اللائحة:' heading before every one of the other 30 articles' regulation content and its complete absence for these 14. Article numbering in this track's keys and law_article_number field refers to the BASE LAW's own article numbers (matching this corpus's established anti_smoking_regulation precedent), not a resequenced 1..30 count.

No legal text is translated, paraphrased, or interpreted. Arabic governs. Read-only over input; deterministic over outputs.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: This track's decree field records Ministerial Resolution No. (4080489) dated 2/1/1439H, per the primary MOH PDF's own cover page ("والئحته التنفيذية الصادرة بالقرار الوزاري رقم (4080489) وتاريخ 1439/1/2هـ") and per the base healthcare_professions_law track's own prior finding. However, this pass independently located a genuinely EARLIER edition of this same consolidated booklet -- nshr.org.sa/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/529_PDF1.pdf, titled 'نظام مزاولة المهن الصحية ولائحته التنفيذية 1432هـ - 2011م' -- which ALREADY contains a full Implementing Regulation (using a different, older paragraph-numbering convention, 'N/Mل' rather than 'N-M') roughly seven years before 2/1/1439H (which corresponds to 2017-09-22, not 2011). This means Resolution 4080489/1439H is very likely a RE-ISSUANCE or CONSOLIDATION of an already-existing regulation into its current (3rd, 1440H/2019) numbering and textual form, rather than the absolute founding resolution that first created an Implementing Regulation under Law article 43 -- directly analogous to this corpus's own prior finding for anti_smoking_regulation, where a superficially 'founding-looking' resolution number was independently shown to be a later amendment. The true founding resolution's own number and date (for the regulation's very first issuance, sometime between the base Law's 1426H enactment and the 2011 nshr copy) were NOT located this pass and are left honestly unconfirmed rather than assumed.

This track's edition-history comparison (2011/1432H nshr.org.sa copy vs. the 2019/1440H '3rd edition' MOH copy ingested here) is NOT an exhaustive, paragraph-by-paragraph diff of all 44 articles' regulation content. What was directly confirmed: the paragraph-numbering CONVENTION changed ('N/Mل' -> 'N-M'); at least one paragraph under law article 2 was renumbered ('9/2ل' in 2011 corresponds to '8-2' in 2019, both reading near-verbatim, implying an insertion/removal/reorder earlier in that article's paragraph list); and the Senior Ulema Council citation under law article 22 (قرار هيئة كبار العلماء رقم 140 وتاريخ 1404/7/29هـ) is stable, verbatim, across both editions. A full systematic diff of all ~106 3rd-edition paragraphs against their 2011 counterparts was not performed this pass; this is disclosed as a scope limitation for a future pass, not silently assumed to be either 'no change' or 'fully compared'.

The primary MOH PDF's embedded font maps the mandatory lam-alef ligature (ل immediately followed by ا) inconsistently in its own ToUnicode/CMap table: at the start of the isolated two-letter negation particle 'لا' it emerges character-swapped as 'ال' (indistinguishable, out of context, from the definite article -- resolved by this track using the fact that every located instance is immediately followed by a verb, never a noun); mid-word, it is dropped outright (e.g. 'علاقة'->'عاقة', 'ثلاثة'->'ثاثة', 'اللائحة'->'الائحة'). Confirmed as a genuine source-file defect (present identically in BOTH independently-produced MOH PDF exports of this regulation, and independent of which extraction tool -- poppler/pdftotext or PyMuPDF -- is used), not an artifact of this track's own extraction choices. Corrected via a small, individually context-verified word list (documented in this track's generator script); every correction only restores a single dropped/reordered ligature letter and changes no other letter, word choice, or legal meaning. A residual risk is honestly disclosed: this word list was built from patterns actually observed in this document's regulation-paragraph text, cross-checked against Arabic dictionary spelling and sentence context, and spot-verified against the second, independently-produced MOH export and rendered page images -- but cannot be claimed as a formally exhaustive proof that zero further instances of this same defect remain undetected in this track's text.

Article 35's third اللائحة paragraph (3-35), in the primary MOH PDF's own page flow, has an editorial footnote (marked '5' in the source) spliced in mid-sentence at a page-break boundary -- the footnote defines the terms 'الدية' (blood money), 'الأرش' (injury compensation) and 'العوض' (indemnity) as used elsewhere in this chapter, in the same style as four other editorial footnotes (marked 1-4) found unambiguously OUTSIDE any اللائحة paragraph, attached instead to the base Law's own text under articles 26-31 (defining المسؤولية المدنية / الخطأ الطبي / المسؤولية الجنائية / المسؤولية التأديبية). This is the MOH booklet compilers' own explanatory annotation apparatus, not part of the operative regulation text itself. It has been excised from paragraph 3-35's adopted text (restoring the paragraph's own uninterrupted sentence: '...ولكل طرف من الأطراف التعقيب على أقوال الطرف الآخر...') and is preserved here, verbatim as extracted, for full transparency: تطلق كلمة (الدية) على المال الذي يقوم الجاني بدفعه للمجني عليه أو لأوليائه عوضاً عن الجناية التي ارتكبها، سواء كانت الجناية على النفس أو على ما دون النفس، إلا أن الفقهاء اصطلحوا على أن يطلقوا (الدية) على العوض الذي يدفعه الجاني بدلاً عن الجناية على النفس، و(الأرش) على العوض الذي يدفعه الجاني بدلاً عن الجروح. الأَرش: وهو جزء من الثمن نسبته ما ينقص العيب من قيمة المبيع لو كان سليما إلى تمام القيمة. يقصد بالعوض: ما يعطى الإنسان بدل ما ذهب منه.

For every article whose اللائحة content happens to be the LAST such content before a فصل/فرع boundary (law articles 4, 14, 23, 25, 41), a naive within-block scrape (bounded only by the next 'المادة' header) would otherwise append the following chapter/section's own heading title text -- and, for article 25 specifically, that heading's own footnote marker ('1', which is itself the start of the separate editorial footnote on 'المسؤولية المدنية' described above) -- onto the article's last regulation paragraph. This is a page-structure scraping artifact, not a content difference; it was identified and trimmed for all five affected articles, directly analogous to this corpus's own prior documented nezams.com article-44 boundary artifact in the base healthcare_professions_law track.

14 of the base Law's 44 articles carry no اللائحة (regulation) paragraph at all in this 3rd edition: articles 6, 13, 21, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 42 and 43. This is confirmed structurally (the 'الالئحة:' heading that unambiguously precedes regulation content for the other 30 articles is simply absent for these 14, in both independently-fetched MOH exports), not an extraction gap. These 14 concentrate almost entirely in the civil/penal/disciplinary-liability chapter (articles 26-32, which the base Law itself defines with unusual self-sufficiency, including its own embedded editorial footnotes rather than a formal اللائحة section) and the closing-provisions chapter (42-43; article 44 does carry one short اللائحة paragraph). This track therefore contains 30 records, not 44 -- consistent with this corpus's established anti_smoking_regulation precedent of ingesting only the law articles that actually carry regulation content, rather than fabricating placeholder records for the rest.

laws.boe.gov.sa (connection reset on direct curl to the domain root; HTTP 503 via WebFetch on the base law's own known lawId page) and ncar.gov.sa (connection reset on direct curl; HTTP 503 via WebFetch on a document-details URL located through web search, whose title -- 'اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الصحية لعام 1439هـ' -- independently corroborates this track's 1439H dating without this track being able to open the page itself) were both unreachable this pass for a live, first-party confirmation of this specific regulation's official record. qanoniah.com's domain root was reachable (HTTP 200) but no page specific to this regulation was individually fetched or confirmed this pass -- consistent with, but not independently re-verifying, this corpus's prior documented finding (anti_smoking_regulation, traffic_regulation) that qanoniah.com gates its actual document text behind client-side JavaScript. r.jina.ai returned HTTP 401 ('bad IP reputation') when tried as a reader-proxy fallback. This track's TIER_2 classification reflects these honestly-disclosed gaps: two independently-fetched official MOH PDF exports (one byte-verified via Wayback Machine and a third-party mirror) plus partial historical corroboration via an older NSHR-hosted edition, but no live BOE/NCAR portal confirmation and no independent non-MOH full-text transcription of the current edition.

**تحفُّظ على سلامة النص**: يحمل 22 سجلاً من 30 في هذا المسار أثر انقلاب رابطة لام-ألف في النص العربي — «االطلاع» موضع «الاطلاع»، و«اإلدارية» موضع «الإدارية»، و«إعالن» موضع «إعلان»، و«الالزمة» موضع «اللازمة».

**وقد تُحقِّق من منشأ هذا الخلل، فهو في ملف المصدر الرسمي نفسه لا في قراءتنا له**: أُعيد جلب ملف الـPDF الذي يستشهد به هذا المسار (https://www.moh.gov.sa/Ministry/Rules/Documents/Executive-Regulations-Health-Profession-1.pdf)، واستُخرج نصّه بأداة مستقلة تماماً عن كل ما بُني به هذا المستودع (poppler/pdftotext) وبأنماط التخطيط الثلاثة جميعها، فظهرت فيه **194** موضعاً من مواضع العطب نفسها. أي أن **الطبقة النصية للملف الرسمي مُرمَّزة هكذا**، ولا يستطيع أي مستخرِج أن يُخرج منها أفضل من ذلك، وأن **النص المخزَّن هنا قراءةٌ أمينة للملف الرسمي**. والصفحة المطبوعة تبدو سليمةً لعين القارئ؛ العطب في ما تقرؤه الآلة وحده. (التحقق: scripts/verify_pdf_source_encoding.py، وتفصيله في reports/corpus_text_integrity_audit/pdf_source_encoding_verification.json)

**وتصويبٌ لما قيل هنا سابقاً**: كان هذا التحفُّظ يقول إن «الجهة نشرت النص سليماً وإن الخلل في النقل». **وذلك خطأ**، قيل قبل إجراء هذا الاختبار، ويناقضه الاختبار.

**ولم يُصحَّح حرف واحد.** الانقلاب **يُحوِّل كلمات عربية صحيحة إلى كلمات عربية صحيحة أخرى**: «العالقة» (المُعلَّقة) قلبُ «العلاقة»، و«عالمة» (التي تعلم) قلبُ «علامة»، و«صالحية» قلبُ «صلاحية» — و«الشوائب **العالقة** ببدن السفينة» و«القضايا **العالقة** لدى المحامين» صوابٌ يقول ما يعنيه. فلا قاعدةَ آليةٌ تفصل العطب عن الصواب؛ الفصل يحتاج الجملة لا الرسم. وجُرِّب إصلاحٌ مشروطٌ بأن يكون الشكل المُصحَّح مشهوداً في نصوص المستودع السليمة فأخفق: الاستخراج يشطر الكلمة أيضاً («خ اال المدة» وأصلها «خلال المدة»)، وبعض «الشواهد» عطبٌ مماثل تسرَّب إلى مسارٍ آخر.

المُفصَح عنه أن **رسم بعض الكلمات في هذه السجلات لا يطابق الرسم الصحيح** وإن بقي المعنى مقروءاً، فلا يصح النسخ الحرفي منها قبل المقابلة بالصفحة المطبوعة. ورفعُ هذا التحفُّظ يكون بنسخٍ بشريٍّ من الصفحة المُصيَّرة، لا بقاعدة ولا بإعادة استخراج. (رصدَه scripts/audit_corpus_text_integrity.py)
